window: Papers published since 4 Oct 2026 (plus two late-September preprints kept for high relevance)
note: Summaries are written by Claude from each paper's abstract. Items marked 'title only' had no abstract available — open the paper before relying on them.

items.title: A Preconditioned Quantum Linear Solver for Periodic Two-Phase Heat Conduction with Mesh-Independent Condition Number

summary.problem: Quantum linear solvers slow down under mesh refinement because the finite element stiffness matrix of a two-phase conduction problem has a condition number that grows quadratically with elements per side.
summary.method: The closed-form inverse square root of the homogeneous operator is folded into the finite element factors so the preconditioned operator has subnormalization one, and QSVT block-encodes its inverse.
summary.result: On three periodic cells with up to 10^6 unknowns the condition number stayed mesh-independent, and Qiskit state-vector runs on 4×4 and 8×8 meshes matched the classical solution within the polynomial tolerance.

items.why: This is the exact obstacle in your quantum pressure solver study and Poisson condition-number note: a two-phase coefficient jump plus mesh refinement drives kappa up. Check whether the homogeneous-operator preconditioning idea survives a 1000:1 density ratio in the variable-density pressure Poisson equation.

items.title: A generalized, quasi-universal subgrid model for macroscopic moving contact line flows
items.authors: V. M. Mundhada, M. K. Tripathi

summary.problem: The no-slip stress singularity at a moving contact line makes macroscopic simulations grid-dependent, and resolving the microscopic scale is unaffordable.
summary.method: Cox's matched-asymptotic relation is coupled with empirical dynamic contact angle models into a subgrid model that needs only a one-time estimate of the observation length scale.
summary.result: Grid-dependence errors dropped across a wide range of Reynolds and Weber numbers for three contact angle models; the abstract gives no specific numbers.

items.why: Directly feeds your proposal's fourth requirement (a contact angle on a moving solid) and the Cox–Voinov/mesh-dependence section; worth testing whether the one-time length scale holds on a translating sphere surface in your three-phase contact line cases.

items.authors: Authors not listed in the journal feed

summary.method: The authors keep the sign in a modified formulation and test both versions in volume-of-fluid simulations of droplet impact and bubble coalescence.
summary.problem: The common Kistler dynamic contact-angle implementation uses the magnitude of the capillary number, so it loses the sign that distinguishes advancing from receding contact lines.
summary.result: The magnitude-based model mispredicts droplet recoil and suppresses bubble detachment, while the corrected model captures both.

items.title: Correcting a capillary-number sign pitfall in Kistler dynamic contact-angle modeling
items.why: Directly relevant to the contact angle on a moving solid in your proposal: during water entry the contact line on the sphere both advances and recedes, so check whether your Kistler/Cox–Voinov implementation keeps the sign of Ca.

summary.method: From the title: a quadratic (curved) interface reconstruction for VOF, paired with a geometric way to extend velocity off the interface.
summary.result: Open the paper to see results.

items.title: Parametrised-Quadratic Interface Reconstruction and Geometric Velocity Extension in the Volume-of-Fluid Framework
items.why: A direct step beyond PLIC: worth comparing against PLIC-Net and your curvature / spurious-current tests, since curved reconstruction is the usual answer to PLIC's curvature error.

items.authors: H. Wu, H. Qi, Y. Zhang et al.

summary.method: Water-entry experiments over a range of cylinder temperatures, entry speeds and diameters, with cavity shapes reconstructed from high-speed images using a Logvinovich-type model.
summary.problem: How does heating a cylinder change the air cavity it opens when it enters water at high speed?
summary.result: A hotter cylinder generally made the cavity grow longer along its axis and delayed pinch-off, while maximum cavity diameter and pinch-off depth changed little (the abstract gives no numbers).

items.title: Experimental study of thermally induced cavity evolution and periodic layered cavities during water entry of heated cylinders
items.why: Heating changes the gas layer and effective wetting at the moving solid, so this is a fresh experimental data set for your proposal's 'contact angle on a moving solid' and 'sub-cell gas layer' requirements, and a possible validation target for the air film in your solver.

items.title: A QSVT-Based Quantum Jacobi Algorithm for Linear Systems with Application to the Poisson Equation
items.authors: L. M. Piskol, T. Grahs, S. Langer

summary.problem: CFD discretizations give large sparse linear systems, yet most quantum solvers aim at full matrix inversion rather than iterative approximation.
summary.method: Each Jacobi iteration is written as a polynomial transformation of a block-encoded operator and implemented with quantum singular value transformation.
summary.result: Ancilla overhead stays constant regardless of iteration count while circuit depth grows linearly; demonstrated on 1D/2D Poisson problems including the Chorin-projection pressure equation for lid-driven cavity flow.

items.why: A projection-method pressure Poisson test case is the closest published analogue to your quantum pressure solver study; an iterative (Jacobi/smoother-style) framing also links naturally to your multigrid discussion.

summary.method: From the title: an interface reconstruction that uses circular arcs and cusps so sharp features are kept instead of smoothed away.
summary.result: Open the paper to see results.

items.title: Feature-preserving interface reconstruction using piecewise circles and cusps
items.why: Sharp corners are exactly what appear where the free surface meets a moving solid at the contact line; check whether its cusp handling could help your three-phase reconstruction cases.

items.title: Accelerating Matrix-Free Fast Diagonalization and Preconditioned Linear Solvers for High-Order Finite Element Discretized Elliptic Problems on Distributed GPUs

summary.problem: High-order finite element elliptic solves on distributed GPUs need both fewer iterations and cheaper iterations.
summary.method: A distributed fast-diagonalization direct Poisson solver is combined with two matrix-free CG preconditioners: p-multigrid with Chebyshev–Jacobi smoothing and a two-level hybrid Schwarz method.
summary.result: The direct solver is 100–1000× faster than Jacobi-preconditioned CG on uniform meshes, and hybrid Schwarz converges in 11 iterations on an octree generalized Poisson problem from 8 to 1024 MI250X GPUs.

items.why: Useful benchmark numbers for the preconditioning part of your Poisson note; the generalized (variable-coefficient) octree case is the nearest to a density-jump pressure equation.

items.title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
items.authors: H. Hao, A. Sergis, M. N. Charalambides

summary.problem: Erosion models for wind turbine blades assume spherical droplets hitting at normal incidence, which rarely happens.
summary.method: Incompressible VOF multiphase simulations are coupled with finite element analysis of the blade material in a fluid-structure interaction model.
summary.result: Peak impact pressure, influential area and peak force are positively correlated while time of peak force scales inversely; a scaling law based on droplet projection area is proposed (no numbers in the abstract).

items.why: A VOF-to-FE partitioned coupling example for impact loading; a handy contrast case for the FSI coupling section of your review, though the solid is fixed rather than moving.

items.title: Droplet-triggered Faraday waves in a vertically forced bath
items.authors: F. T. Mahmood, C. R. Constante-Amores

summary.problem: Repeated droplet impacts can trigger a growing Faraday-wave response even when the undisturbed bath is linearly stable.
summary.method: Axisymmetric two-phase DNS over a wide range of Reynolds and Weber numbers, supported by Floquet analysis and a Bessel decomposition of the bath response.
summary.result: The switch to the unstable-bath regime happens over a comparatively narrow Weber-number range and depends only weakly on Reynolds number (no numbers in the abstract).

items.why: Shows how impact-driven capillary waves near the air film evolve on a deforming pool; a good reference for droplet/bubble dynamics framing in job talks.
